question: Do context-induced alias classes remain useful when unseen multi-step role programs switch raw surface families across operations?
hypothesis: Using the unchanged multistep scientific function with single-step transition training only, the induced-class learner will achieve at least 0.95 accuracy on all 192 frozen three-, five-, and seven-step mixed-alias programs, while exact-surface and shuffled-bridge controls remain at or below 0.25 overall accuracy.

prior_qualified_evidence.observation: A third surface family with zero task-transition examples achieved 1.0 task accuracy through contextual alias classes; exact-surface scored 0.0625 and shuffled-context 0.05.

validity_criteria: Exact parent and North Star identities match.

Evaluator operation semantics generate and score targets only.
Full Go regression passes before probe execution and all metrics are finite.
No tokenizer, external model, network call, capacity growth, threshold change, or adaptive evaluation occurs.
